title: Modernize CI: introduce task graph, per-job dep isolation, and toolchain pinning
author: Anika Shah
description: Context: our current GitHub Actions matrix runs large monolithic jobs which cause long queuing times, brittle cache keys, and repeated work across similar tasks. Motivation: reduce CI minutes, make failure modes easier to triage, enable incremental execution, and provide deterministic toolchains for reproducible builds. This PR introduces a lightweight task-graph runner for our CI pipelines, decomposes the large matrix into smaller named tasks (checkout -> bootstrap -> lint -> unit-test -> integration-smoke -> build-artifacts -> publish), and adds per-job dependency isolation + lock verification to prevent dependency drift. To improve reproducibility we pin the LLVM/rust/node toolchain snippets used in native builds and add a per-PR toolchain override for emergency rollbacks. The description below summarizes the surface changes, migration notes, and testing performed. Features: 1) CI task graph YAML templates: new .github/ci/task-graph.yml and reusable job templates under .github/ci/templates/*.yml so individual repos can opt-in to the graph. 2) Task runner shim: a small Go binary tools/ci/graph-runner that interprets the graph and enforces parallelism/ordering and exit semantics (used only in Actions runner). 3) Per-job virtualenvs and node_modules caches keyed by repository+lockfile-hash to reduce cross-PR cache contamination. 4) Dependency lock verification step: CI now fails fast if installed deps diverge from lockfile; an opt-out for legacy branches exists. 5) Toolchain pin manifests: .ci/toolchains.yaml with pinned versions and a small bootstrap script .ci/setup-toolchain that fetches exact versions for llvm/clang/rustup/node. 6) Release artifact naming standardized to redwood-<repo>-<commit>-<platform>.zip to make downstream publishing idempotent. Migration: the change is opt-in — older repos will continue to use the matrix until maintainers flip the workflow reference. Rollout plan: opt-in for core redwood packages this week, monitor CI minutes and flaky tests, then expand to SDK repos. Testing: validated against redwood/core, redwood-sdk-python, and redwood-helm-charts in a dogfood run. Observed ~34% reduction in total runner minutes for the core repo and fewer cache misses. See commits and files changed for details.
commits: Add task-graph templates and example graphs for core repo
Implement tools/ci/graph-runner (Go) + unit tests for graph scheduling
Introduce per-job dependency isolation + cache key strategy
Add .ci/toolchains.yaml and setup-toolchain script; pin llvm/rust/node versions
Add lock verification step and opt-out mechanism for legacy branches
Docs: migration guide and FAQ for switching to task graph
review_comments: Marco Bell: Nice decomposition — two asks: (1) can we tighten the default per-task timeout to 20m for lint/unit to avoid runaway jobs? (2) please document how cache key rotation works for infra ops.
Anika Shah (author): lowered lint/unit default timeout to 20m, added TTL config for caches in .github/ci/task-graph.yml and documented cache rotation in docs/ci/migration-to-task-graph.md
Sofia Nguyen: graph-runner looks good but please add a health endpoint or verbose logs when a step is stuck to aid debugging in Actions logs.
Anika Shah: added verbose --debug flag and a simple /metrics/prometheus endpoint behind a local-only listener for e2e debugging; documented invocation in README of tools/ci
Evan Park: CI flakiness triage -- we should surface flaky test metadata into PR checks so maintainers can see historical flakiness per test. Recommend a follow-up (ENG-3499).
Anika Shah: ACK; added ENG-3499 to linked_linear for flaky-test telemetry follow-up
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (matrix reduced to per-package jobs)
release_notes: Opt-in CI task-graph + per-job dep isolation; pinned toolchains (LLVM/Rust/Node) for reproducible builds; lockfile verification added; standardized release artifact naming. No runtime behavior changes to production services.
notes_for_ops: Operators: toolchain pins live in .ci/toolchains.yaml; to temporarily override a pinned toolchain for emergency builds set CI_TOOLCHAIN_OVERRIDE env on the runner. Cache keys are now keyed by <repo>-<lock-hash>-<package-manager>-<platform>. If you need to evict caches manually use the 'ci:evict-cache' Makefile target which calls the cache API with prefix matching.
backout_plan: If the graph introduces regressions, revert by changing workflow refs back to the legacy matrix (branch: main) and re-enable the previous matrix workflow copy located at .github/workflows/ci-legacy.yml. A temporary feature flag CI_FORCE_LEGACY=true is supported to force the legacy path per-run.
testing_summary: Dogfood runs against core packages + SDKs across linux/ubuntu-latest and macos-latest. Measured a 34% reduction in total runner minutes for core package; cache hit rate improved from ~52% to ~78%. No regressions in smoke integration runs. Observability: added basic traces for task durations to be ingested into existing tracing pipeline.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Enable task-graph workflow for redwood/sdk repos over next 48 hours. 2) Run dependency lock enforcement on the weekly maintenance cron to surface legacy drift. 3) Follow-up ENG-3499 for flaky-test telemetry.
changelog_entry: ci: introduce task-graph runner, per-job dep isolation, toolchain pinning, lockfile verification
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: the graph-runner is used only as an orchestration shim inside Actions and does not replace our internal runners. We kept an opt-out path to minimize disruption to release automation while enabling fast iteration on cache and parallelism strategies.
